device.name: Keithley 2230G multi-channel power supply

facts.text: The upstream README says the author used National Instruments VISA and could not test the code on the instrument
The clone imports visa and defines the device class KEI2230G
The constructor takes inst_address but opens self.instr_address, which it never sets
get_info queries *IDN? and splits the reply on commas into manufacturer, model, serial and firmware
Channel selection writes INST:NSEL with a channel number validated to range(1, 4)
The set_volt body contains VOLT command text for the selected channel
The set_curr body contains CURR command text for the selected channel
The voltage readback body contains VOLT? query text
A current setpoint is queried as CURR?
The selected channel output is set with CHAN:OUTP
The selected channel output is queried with CHAN:OUTP?
All channel outputs are set with OUTP
All channel outputs are queried with OUTP?
A fresh voltage measurement is requested with MEAS:VOLT? on a named channel
A fresh current measurement is requested with MEAS:CURR? on a named channel
get_model documents the model types 30-3, 30-6 and 60-3
The model-specific branches compare the bound method self.get_model to the string '30-3', so they never run
The voltage readback method calls the misspelt self.inst.quert, so that method is broken
The error queue is queried with SYST:ERR?
The output protection state is cleared with OUTP:PROT:CLE

operator_required.name: voltage_setpoint_ch1
operator_required.reason: The 2230G can be a 30-3, 30-6 or 60-3 (2230G.py:84), and the clone gives different CH1/CH2 voltage bounds per model (2230G.py:568-652). The model guard compares get_model without calling it (2230G.py:568), and the installed model is not known at load time; the operator supplies the voltage bound of the actual unit.
